The patient ticks that it was explained, or chooses Ask the dentist first, and the dentist confirms on the record." §7 evidence line "Signed on their phone 10:42", with the attestation recorded later; the timestamps prove the signature came first. §5.2 suggestConsents reads "the visit's catalog_id row" and returns preTick. The general consent already in force says the opposite: src/lib/patient-forms-def.ts:222 "Before any treatment starts, the dentist explains what they suggest and why, the other choices, the cost, and what could go wrong. Nothing starts until you agree to it." and :227 "to treatment once the dentist has explained it to me". PDA consent (scratchpad pda_consent.png): "consent to have any treatment done by the dentist after the procedure, the risks & benefits & cost have been fully explained". Li v. Soliman, G.R. No. 165279, 7 Jun 2011: the physician has a duty to disclose material risks, and failure to disclose is element 2 of the action (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/1/37801).
objections.fix: Explain, then confirm, then sign. For a new patient, or any procedure a dentist has not yet set, the QR carries page 1, the general consent and privacy (and photos). Procedure forms ticked in the checklist are prepared, and the patient sees them as "Read before you see the dentist" with no signature control. They become signable only once the named dentist has set the clinical part and pressed "I explained this" (an attestation row written before the signing). The patient then signs at the chair on the tablet, or on the same link if it is still open. intake_decide refuses agreed/refused on a procedure document with no attestation. The phone may carry procedure pages only when a treating dentist already recorded them as an accepted plan item at an earlier visit. suggestConsents should pre-tick from accepted plan items only and list a booking reason as "Patient booked for: extraction (not yet examined)", unticked. Take the patient tick "it was explained to me" off any page without an attestation. Put §10.2 back to the owner with this as the default.

objections.problem: The tablet path opens page 1 in production under privacy-2026-09. Page 1 is the forms' full health step and details (address, emergency contact, a parent's details, PhilHealth PIN, Facebook), and it takes a patient-ticked privacy consent. That is exactly the situation the repo closed the QR forms over: consent to sensitive personal information must be informed, and the notice in force does not name these things. Which device the patient types on does not change what they are agreeing to. The spec itself concedes that the new notice must name "what page 1 collects, the 24-hour and 30-day deletions and the signed forms".
objections.evidence: CLAUDE.md:678-690 ("Closed in production until the privacy notice covers it … privacy-2026-09 does not name what the forms collect … RA 10173 s.13(a)"). src/lib/patient-forms.ts:24-26 and :144-148 (FORMS_PRIVACY_VERSIONS is empty). src/pages/privacy.astro:60-64: "What we keep" lists only name and mobile, the visit, and the clinic's record; :113 still has the placeholders [YOUR DPO NAME] and [YOUR DPO EMAIL]. Spec §5.5 row "Here, on this device: open"; §10.7 "default open, as today's Add patient"; build order 5. RA 10173 s.3(b) and s.13(a) (https://privacy.gov.ph/data-privacy-act/).
objections.fix: Put page 1 behind one gate, formsNoticeReady, on every device. In production, until the notice is listed, the intake runs consents only: patients on file, or a new patient whose details the desk types at /new/type/ with desk consent, then the consent pages on the tablet. The privacy screen is not offered and nothing patient-typed is stored. Alternatively, cut INTAKE_DEF page 1 in production to the fields the notice in force names. Add a test to §9 item 15: tablet plus production shows no page 1.

objections.problem: The privacy tick on page 1 records only privacy_version and privacy_at. §4.1 turns it into a patient_consent row with recorded_by set to the adder, and nothing says who agreed or in what capacity. For a minor, a yaya, a driver or the child can tick it, and it is stored as the patient's consent. Every other channel in the repo requires agreed_as plus a named guardian.
objections.evidence: Spec SQL intake_save_page1: `privacy_version = case when p_screen = 'privacy' then p_privacy …, privacy_at = …now()`, with no signer. §4.1: "channel intake, intake_id, given_at = intake.privacy_at and recorded_by set to the adder". src/data/migrations/021_patient_health.sql:51-53 (desk: agreed_as not null and a name unless the patient). src/data/migrations/028_patient_forms.sql:229-230 (form: recorded_by, agreed_as and given_by_name required).
objections.fix: The privacy screen asks who is agreeing: the patient, or a parent or guardian with name, relation and authority. The same authority rules as intake_decide apply, so a minor needs someone with authority. Store the answer on intake (privacy_by_name, privacy_as, privacy_relation, privacy_authority). The 'intake' channel check in 039 requires agreed_as and given_by_name, as 'form' does. If a minor has nobody with authority present, page 1 still saves, the privacy consent stays "not given", and the desk sees it.

objections.problem: Substitute authority is accepted on any free-text note of 1–200 characters, so "Mama at work" lets any adult who brought the child sign an extraction. Under the Family Code, substitute parental authority arises only when the parents or a judicial guardian are in default. It follows a fixed order, and the sibling must be the oldest one over 21. The spec's list ("brother or sister over 21, the adult caring for the child when the parents are absent") misstates both points. Nobody's age is captured, although two of the three categories require over 21. "A parent" is also treated as always having authority, but a child born outside marriage is under the mother's authority, and with separated parents it is the parent the court designates.
objections.evidence: Spec SQL intake_decide: `v_auth in ('substitute','representative') and (v_note is null or char_length(v_note) > 200)` is the only check. §10.13 wording. Family Code (EO 209) Art. 216: "In default of parents or a judicially appointed guardian … in the order indicated: (1) The surviving grandparent … (2) The oldest brother or sister, over twenty-one years of age … (3) The child's actual custodian, over twenty-one years of age". Art. 214: "death, absence or unsuitability of the parents". Art. 176: "Illegitimate children … shall be under the parental authority of their mother". Art. 213: separated parents, "the parent designated by the Court" (scratchpad fc.html; https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo1987/eo_209_1987.html).
objections.fix: Replace the free note with the Art. 214/216 ground (parents have died, are absent with whereabouts unknown, or are unfit or under a court order) and the category in its order, plus a required tick "I am 21 or older" for categories 2 and 3. A parent who is simply not here today is not substitute authority. The clinic takes a written authorisation from the parent (a photo in Files, named in authority_note and confirmed by the desk), or the page waits as To sign. Substitute authority cannot be completed on the phone link alone: it needs the desk's confirmation on the tablet, or paper. The lawyer settles the words of "A parent" (Arts. 176 and 213) before CONSENT_REVIEWED lists any form.

objections.section: §8 "An adult who cannot sign", intake_decide adult authority
objections.problem: Two different cases are treated as one. An adult who cannot write (illiterate, injured hand, stroke with capacity intact) still decides for themselves. An adult who cannot decide needs a legal representative. The spec's answer to both is that a relative signs as 'representative' with a free-text reason, self-declared on the patient's phone, and nobody records that the patient lacks capacity. That takes the decision away from competent adults. There is also no 'court_guardian' choice for adults, although a court-appointed guardian of an incompetent adult is the one clear legal authority.
objections.evidence: Spec SQL intake_decide: for a non-minor, `array['representative']` is the only authority, plus a note. §8: "An adult who cannot sign: a representative signs, with relation and reason." RA 10173 s.3(b): consent "may also be given on behalf of the data subject by an agent specifically authorized by the data subject". Civil Code Art. 1327(2), on who cannot give consent (scratchpad civil.html). The 2004 Rules on Notarial Practice (A.M. No. 02-8-13-SC), Rule IV s.1(b)–(c), are the Philippine pattern for a signature by thumbmark, or by another at the person's direction, before disinterested witnesses (https://lawphil.net/courts/supreme/am/am_02-8-13-sc_2004.html). Rules of Court Rules 92–93 cover guardianship of incompetents.
objections.fix: Split the path in two. (a) The patient decides but cannot write: signed_as stays 'patient', with method 'mark' (the patient's mark or thumb on the pad, or a staff member signs at the patient's direction), and the staff member who watched is named as witness by their own tap. Tablet only. (b) The patient cannot decide: allow 'court_guardian' for adults. A 'representative' is allowed only after the dentist has recorded on the patient's record that the patient cannot decide and why, and only on the tablet or paper, never the phone link. The lawyer confirms the categories.

objections.problem: The photos consent cannot be refused: the definer answers 'invalid' to anything but 'agreed'. A patient who does not want photos can only press "Ask the dentist first" ('later'). That alerts the desk, and after Send the record shows the form as "To sign", so the clinic will keep asking. That is pressure attached to a refusal. Consent under the Data Privacy Act must be freely given and granular, and publication use (the website, social media) is a new purpose the current notice says will not happen without asking.
objections.evidence: Spec SQL: `or (v.code = 'photos' and p_decision <> 'agreed') then raise exception using errcode = 'check_violation'`. §8: "Ask the dentist first … After Send it is To sign on the record". NPC Circular 2023-04: consent is not freely given where there is a "possibility of adverse consequences for refusal"; "withdrawing consent is as easy as, if not easier than, giving consent"; "The consent given must be granular" (https://privacy.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/NPC-Circular-No.-2023-04_Guidelines-on-Consent_07Nov2023.pdf, quoted via https://admprivacy.org/2024/01/02/summary-npc-circular-no-2023-04-guidelines-on-consent/). src/pages/privacy.astro:68-70 says "No marketing, and no use for a new purpose without asking you first."
objections.fix: Give the photos page "Yes" with per-use ticks, none pre-ticked (teaching or case reports, the clinic's website or social media), and "No, thank you". A no is stored as 'refused' with no signature required, shows on the record as "No photos for publication" rather than "To sign", and raises no desk alert. Clinical photos for the record stay under the general consent's Examination point (and s.13(e)), not this page. Say on the page how to withdraw: tell the clinic in person, by phone or by text.

objections.section: §7 head chips, §10.10 "nothing is blocked by it yet"
objections.problem: A signed refusal, a withdrawal, an unsigned form, or a dentist who has not confirmed is only a chip on the record. Mark done on the plan item, and the visit's In the chair and Done steps, go ahead with no question. Treating after a documented refusal is the worst possible record for the clinic. The repo already asks first for a less serious gap (a missing LOA).
objections.evidence: Spec §7 (chips "Not agreed: Tooth extraction", "To sign") and §10.10. CLAUDE.md:884 (034, HMO LOA): "A plan item waiting for its LOA says so and Mark done asks first."
objections.fix: Link each procedure document to its plan item or visit, and have Mark done, In the chair (/api/schedule) and the VisitStrip's done lines ask first when that document is refused, withdrawn, to sign or not confirmed: "The patient did not agree to Tooth extraction · 36 on 29 Sep. Record it anyway?" The dentist types a reason, audited as consent.override. It is not a hard block, because of emergencies.

objections.problem: On the phone path the person who made the link did not see the signing. The patient signs in the waiting room, or anywhere within the link's life. Naming that person as the witness puts a false statement on a medico-legal document, and it fails the first time that staff member is asked about it.
objections.evidence: Spec §10.11: "The staff member who made the link is recorded as the witness in the evidence line." §8: the link lives until 20 minutes idle, with drafts kept 24 hours, so signing happens away from the desk.
objections.fix: Record facts only: "Link made by Liza Santos 10:31 · signed on the patient's phone 10:42". Where a witness matters (the tablet at the chair, signature by mark, guardian cases), the staff member who actually watched taps "I saw this signed" under their own session, and that is stored as the witness. The dentist's attestation is the clinic's own signature on the form.

objections.problem: Both hashes are computed by a trigger in the same database that stores the row, and verifySigning recomputes them there too. Anyone who can rewrite a consent_signing row (Flossify's operators with the owner role, a restored or edited backup) can also recompute its hashes. The green "Matches its fingerprint" then proves nothing against the parties who could alter the record. The e-signature statute requires the procedure to be "not alterable by the parties interested". The patient also leaves with nothing to compare against.
objections.evidence: Spec SQL intake_send: `repeat('0', 64), repeat('0', 64) … (the zeros are placeholders: consent_signing_check computes both fingerprints)`; §5.1 verifySigning "recomputes both hashes in SQL with consent_seal"; §10.15, the patient's copy is "printed at the desk". RA 8792 s.8: "a prescribed procedure, not alterable by the parties interested in the electronic document, existed under which – (a) A method is used to identify the party …" (scratchpad ecom.html; https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2000/ra_8792_2000.html).
objections.fix: Chain the seals per clinic, so each seal includes the previous signing's seal, and anchor the chain outside the database. Show a short seal (10 characters) to the patient on the thank-you page when the phone is their own, and print it on their copy. Print the day's chain head on Close the day and send it to the owner. Word the check as "Unchanged since it was stored" unless it is checked against the patient's copy or the chain head.

objections.section: §10.5 Filipino, §5.5 "Filipino lines only for langs including fil"
objections.problem: Risks and alternatives are shown in full English only, with a few Filipino key lines, and the general consent stays English-only. Many patients, for example at a Baguio clinic (Ilocano) or in Cebu, will be told the risks in another language. The form never records which language the explanation was given in, or who read it to the patient. Under Philippine law, when a party cannot read or does not understand the language of the document, the clinic must prove the terms were fully explained.
objections.evidence: Spec §10.5 and §5.5. Civil Code Art. 1332: "When one of the parties is unable to read, or if the contract is in a language not understood by him, and mistake or fraud is alleged, the person enforcing the contract must show that the terms thereof have been fully explained to the former." (scratchpad civil.html; https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1949/ra_386_1949.html).
objections.fix: On every consent page, record "Explained to me in: English / Filipino / Ilocano / Cebuano / other ___" and "I read it myself / It was read to me by ___ (staff)". Put the language in the dentist's attestation too, and print both on the document and in the snapshot.

objections.section: §5.2 checklist ("whitening refused for a minor on file"), intake_decide (v_birth from answers)
objections.problem: For a new patient, whether they are a minor comes only from the birth date typed on the phone. The desk, which can see the patient, is never asked before the QR. A 16-year-old who types 2005 signs everything himself, and a whitening form prepared for a new minor is caught only at signing. There it comes back as a generic 'invalid', which leaves the parent at a dead end unless they find "Ask the dentist first". A child who came alone, or with a yaya, gets a QR for pages nobody present can sign.
objections.evidence: Spec §5.2 checklist row: "whitening refused for a minor on file" (on file only). SQL: `v_birth := case when target = 'new' then (answers ->> 'birth_date')::date …`; whitening for a minor raises check_violation, which returns 'invalid'. The 'later' branch skips the signer checks, so the only way through is 'later'. §8 bullets on the yaya.
objections.fix: The checklist (Screen B) for a new patient asks two questions. "Under 18?" (yes / no / not sure) and "Who came with them?" (a parent / a guardian / someone else / nobody). If under 18, whitening is not offered and the guardian section is forced. If someone else or nobody came, procedure pages are not prepared and page 1 goes without privacy. If the typed birth date contradicts the desk's answer, the page stops and says "Please ask the desk", and the desk sees why. When page 1 makes the patient a minor, cancel any whitening document (with an intake_event) instead of answering 'invalid'.

objections.problem: An intake that was sent but never added is deleted after 30 days, and its signings go with it. A new walk-in is usually created as a stub through "Here now" and treated on that stub. If the desk never presses Add, the intake is never joined to the stub, and 30 days later the only signed consent for a procedure that was done is gone. The chairside screens never show the dentist that signed forms exist.
objections.evidence: Spec SQL retention_purge: `or (status = 'sent' and sent_at < now() - interval '30 days')`, then `delete from consent_signing … d.patient_id is null`. CLAUDE.md:937 (walk-in, "Here now"). Spec §8: "A walk-in stub from 'Here now' is found as a look-alike and filled." §10.1: Add is a separate desk tap.
objections.fix: Never purge a sent intake that holds an agreed or refused signing while a patient row matches it (same name and birth date, or the stub linked from the visit). When a visit's patient matches a sent intake, show "Forms sent, not added: add them now" on the VisitStrip, the visit panel and In the chair, and ask first before In the chair. The purge deletes only intakes with no signings, or with a signed intake and no match after 30 days. The new notice's 30-day sentence must match this rule.

objections.problem: The procedure templates are gated on review in production, but the general consent is exempt (`t.code === ('general' as never)`). The one form every new patient signs is the one form allowed through unreviewed. treatment-2026-09 is still on the list of words a dentist and the lawyer have not read.
objections.evidence: Spec §5.1 `offered = … || t.code === ('general' as never)`, and §5.5 row "Templates: … general always". CLAUDE.md:1038-1042: "The consent to examination and treatment (treatment-2026-09) is Flossify's plain summary … a dentist and the lawyer read it too" (under "Open — read before shipping").
objections.fix: Put 'general' into Code and into CONSENT_REVIEWED like every other template, and remove the exemption. Until treatment-2026-09 is listed, the intake's general page refuses in production just as procedures do. Or, if the owner accepts the risk for the existing 035 page, record that as the owner's decision in CLAUDE.md, not in a cast.

objections.section: §5.2 Go live row, §5.5 tablet "the desk's own browser"
objections.problem: This slows the front desk. The QR cannot go live until every document's clinic part is complete (dentist, teeth, estimate, explanation fields for each form), so a walk-in stands at the desk through three screens before typing anything. In production the only open path is "Here, on this device", which parks the desk's own browser for the whole of page 1 plus three consent pages. A clinic with one front-desk computer loses its calendar, calls and payments for 10–15 minutes per new patient.
objections.evidence: Spec §5.2 Go live: "every document valid (re-read)". §5.5: "Here, on this device — open (claimed at hand-over by the desk's own browser; a phone cannot take it)". §10.7: the phone path waits in production. §5.1 park.ts: readSession returns null while fl_park is present.
objections.fix: Go live straight after the checklist. Page 1 needs nothing from the clinic's part, and a consent page shows "The clinic is still preparing this form" until it is saved (the doc_rev mechanism already handles later changes). Let "Here, on this device" hand over to a separate signed-in clinic tablet, which enters a six-character desk code, so the desk computer is never parked.

objections.problem: The clinical content the patient signs (the procedure, the tooth, the alternatives and specific risks chosen) can be filled in by anyone with records.edit. By default that includes the secretary and the dental assistant, before any exam. Only the attestation is restricted to the dentist. A receptionist typing "36" from a booking note into a signed extraction consent invites a wrong-site extraction.
objections.evidence: src/lib/can.ts:40-41: the secretary and dental assistant hold 'records.edit'. Spec §5.2 checks only canEditRecords for saveClinicPart; "attestMine only where dentist_id = staffId". §9 flow 1: "extraction 36. The clinic's part prefills from the fee guide".
objections.fix: Split the clinic's part in two. The desk sets the dentist, the visit and the estimate. The clinical fields (procedure, teeth, alternatives, specific risks) are set or confirmed only by a staff member who treats and holds a PRC licence, stored as fields_set_by and fields_set_at on consent_document. Until then the page renders "Tooth: to be confirmed by the dentist" and cannot be signed.

objections.problem: "Record a paper signing" does not require the scan. The record then shows the form as signed on the say-so of one staff member, with no signature image, and "with the scan in Files" is left to memory.
objections.evidence: Spec §5.2 row "Record a paper signing": the checks are paper_printed_at and signedOn only. §8: "Paper is the fallback … with the scan in Files".
objections.fix: recordPaperSigning takes the attachment id of the scanned page (this patient, uploaded after paper_printed_at). Or, until one is attached, the document shows an amber "Signed on paper, scan missing" chip, and the pill always says "Signed on paper".

objections.problem: When as = 'patient', the signer's name is free text with no link to the patient. An adult patient "Juan dela Cruz" can have a form reading "Signed by: Maria Santos, as the patient". That weakens the identification an e-signature relies on (RA 8792 s.8(a)).
objections.evidence: Spec SQL: `v_name := btrim(p_signer ->> 'name')`, checked only for length and against the snapshot.
objections.fix: When as = 'patient', the server takes the name from page 1 or the record and shows it read-only. Only a guardian, representative or mark witness types a name.

objections.problem: "Read for 2 min 10 s" is decided_at minus opened_at, which is the time the page was open, not time spent reading. As evidence it overstates what is known.
objections.evidence: Spec SQL: `greatest(0, extract(epoch from (p.decided_at - p.opened_at))::integer)`; §7 "read for 2 min 10 s".
objections.fix: Word it "page open 2 min 10 s before deciding".

objections.problem: For a patient on file, whoever scans the desk QR first sees the patient's name, procedure, tooth and dentist, and can sign as them. On a desk screen facing a queue, that is health information shown to a stranger.
objections.evidence: Spec §8: "Two phones scan the same code: the first Start wins." §5.3: the token alone opens the door; target 'existing' names the patient from the start.
objections.fix: For target 'existing', the first screen asks for the patient's birth date (or the last four digits of the mobile on file) before showing any name or form. Three misses retire the link as 'replaced', and the desk panel says so.

objections.problem: In production the tablet path is left open for new patients, before the privacy notice covers what page 1 collects. That skips the 028 gate. Page 1 is the forms' whole health step (Q6), which includes pregnancy, birth control and alcohol or drug use, plus contact fields built from FIELDS (Facebook). The patient ticks privacy-2026-09 for all of it. The 028 rule closes exactly this collection-plus-own-tick in production, whatever the device is. The spec admits the gap in Q14: 'The new privacy notice must say the last two'.
objections.evidence: CLAUDE.md:678 ('Closed in production until the privacy notice covers it … RA 10173 s.13(a)'). src/lib/patient-forms.ts:133-148 (FORMS_PRIVACY_VERSIONS names health history, address, emergency contact, a parent's details, Facebook; the list is empty). patient-forms-def.ts:341 (facebook), 398 (alcohol_drugs), 404 (pregnant), 406 (birth_control). Today's typed Add patient collects only allergies, conditions, medications and a note (health.ts:176-193). Spec §5.5 row 'Here, on this device | open' and Q7 'default open, as today's Add patient'.
objections.fix: Gate every target:'new' intake (page 1) on formsNoticeReady(privacy in force) for both devices: startIntake and goLive refuse it, and lookupIntake answers 'unavailable'. In production before the new notice, offer only consents-only intakes for a patient on file. The desk types the person in on /new/type/, then uses 'Prepare consent forms'. This is what 035 already does live. Replace Q7's default with this.

objections.problem: Parking is only a cookie the browser holds. The staff member's fl_session stays valid on the handed-over device, and readSession hides it only while fl_park is present. fl_park expires after 24 h, but a 'My own' session lasts 14 days. A tablet left parked overnight reopens the whole workspace, with no password, to whoever picks it up next. On a desk computer ('Here, on this device'), a patient can also delete fl_park in DevTools and get the same result.
objections.evidence: auth.ts:47 SESSION_HOURS.own = 14 days and :54 (fl_session maxAge follows). Spec §5.1: fl_park '{ s, c, i, exp: +24 h }', and 'readSession … returns null while a valid fl_park is present'. Sessions are stateless HMAC cookies with no server-side session to mark as parked (auth.ts header).
objections.fix: At hand-over, sign the device out: call clearSession() and bump nothing. Keep fl_park only as a hint (who, which clinic, which intake) so the unlock page can prefill the person and go back to the intake. The spec already requires the password to unlock (Q12), so nothing is lost. Also drop the allowParked branch from readSession.

objections.section: 8 'A patient types a /c/ address on a parked tablet' / hand-over
objections.problem: The hand-over does not clear what the workspace already left on the device. (1) The service worker keeps a copy of the last record whose chart was open, for up to 4 h. It drops that copy only on a POST to /auth/ or /start/, or on a visit to /auth/. The hand-over POSTs to /c/…/patients/intake/<id>/, so the copy survives. It is served for that record's address whenever the network is down or takes more than 5 s, so the parked tablet can show another patient's record in a brownout. (2) Other tabs that are already open with workspace pages stay rendered, and an open chart keeps accepting changes. requireWorkspace only guards new requests.
objections.evidence: public/sw.js:63 (RECORD_PAGE), :66 (RECORD_WAIT_MS = 5000), :67-68 (SESSION_POST and AUTH_PAGE cover /auth and /start only), :201-217 (recordNavigation serves the copy on a failure or a timeout), :283 (forgetSession runs only for SESSION_POST). src/lib/offline-queue.ts:339 (the 'flossify-offline' BroadcastChannel).
objections.fix: Send the hand-over through a path the SW treats as a session change (for example POST /auth/park/, which then redirects to /f/i/<token>/), or give sw.js a PARK rule that runs forgetSession(). Put unlock under /auth/ (/auth/unlock/) so AUTH_PAGE drops the copy there too. Before navigating, the hand-over page posts {who:null} and a 'parked' message on the BroadcastChannel. Clinic.astro listens for it and replaces its content with a locked cover that links to unlock. Add a check to §9 that parks in brownout mode and navigates back.

objections.problem: The definers as written never lock the intake. They read status from intake_gate's composite and then write unconditionally. The final `update intake set status = v_done … where id = i.id` has no `and status = 'out'` guard. Two concurrent Sends are a double tap on 3G, and two check-page renders carry different nonces. Both pass the 'open'/'out' checks, both insert a consent_signing per page, and the second UPDATE simply waits and then overwrites. The same happens when a desk cancelIntake races Send: a cancelled intake can become 'sent'/'added' with signings, or a sent one can become 'cancelled' and be purged after 24 h. A page-1 save that resets pages (resign) can also race intake_decide, so a signature made against stale patient details survives.
objections.evidence: Spec intake_send: `i := g.v_intake; … if i.status <> 'out' …; insert into consent_signing …; update intake set status = v_done … where id = i.id`. No FOR UPDATE appears in any shown definer, and consent_signing has no stated unique key. By contrast, the desk side locks (§5.2 step 5), as does 028's lockForm (patient-forms.ts:476-481, `for update`).
objections.fix: Make intake_gate's first statement `select … from intake where id = … for update` (and lock the link row), and document that every volatile definer depends on it. Add `and status = 'out'` to intake_send's final UPDATE and check its row count. Add a unique index on consent_signing (intake_id, document_id) where intake_id is not null. cancelIntake and stopLink take the same row lock (they already do via §5.2 step 5).

objections.section: 8 'Words in force change mid-way' / intake_send stale CTE
objections.problem: When the words in force change, the patient hits a dead end. intake_decide returns 'changed' whenever consent_document.version_id is not the version in force, and nothing ever points a document at the new version. intake_send's stale CTE wipes the patient's signatures and returns 'changed', but the pages can never be signed again, so §8's 'the affected pages redraw with the new words to sign again' cannot happen. At the desk, saveChecklist creates documents only for newly ticked codes, so a ticked code keeps its stale document. 'Prepare it again' has no operation behind it. Phase 5 plans new versions (040+) after the lawyer's review, so every intake in flight will hit this at least once.
objections.evidence: Spec intake_decide: `if d.version_id is distinct from (case v.kind … current_document_of(v.code)).id end) then return 'changed'`. intake_send: the `stale` CTE resets intake_page only. §5.2 Checklist: 'creates a document per new code …, cancels unticked unsigned ones'. §8 'redraw with the new words'.
objections.fix: Add a desk operation, renewDocuments (or a branch in saveChecklist). It cancels each unsigned document whose version is no longer in force and creates a successor at the version in force. It copies fields when the template's field set is unchanged, and otherwise returns the document to the clinic's-part step. On the phone, 'changed' should say 'The clinic updated this form; please ask the desk', not 'sign again'. intake_send should not wipe pages it cannot re-offer.

objections.problem: The purge deletes consent_document rows before the intake, while intake_page and intake_event rows that reference document_id still exist. It then deletes intakes whose documents stay on a patient's record, and those documents still reference the intake. Unless every one of these FKs is ON DELETE CASCADE (intake_page and intake_event → consent_document) or SET NULL (consent_document.intake_id), the function raises. Because it is a single function, one failure also stops the 2-year text purge and the 30-day forms purge that the privacy notice promises. The worker only logs the failure.
objections.evidence: Spec retention_purge order: delete attestation → signing → consent_document → intake. intake_mark_page and intake_decide insert intake_event rows that carry document_id. The spec says documents for a patient on file 'stay on the record'. scripts/sms/worker.ts:138 catches the error and only logs 'retention pass failed'. CLAUDE.md: 'The privacy notice promises text logs go after two years; retention_purge() … keep that true'.
objections.fix: State the FKs explicitly in 039: consent_document.intake_id ON DELETE SET NULL, and intake_page/intake_event/intake_link → intake ON DELETE CASCADE. Delete the children first and explicitly (intake_event, intake_page, intake_link where intake_id = any(v_ids)) before the documents. Wrap the intake block in its own BEGIN … EXCEPTION sub-block so the message_log and patient_form deletes always run. Return the per-kind counts.

objections.section: 5.2 Start vs 8 'A form refused by the patient'
objections.problem: The spec contradicts itself on re-signing. §8 (and the document page's actions in §7) say that after a refusal or a withdrawal the dentist uses 'Sign on this tablet' on the same document, producing a new signing where the latest counts. But startIntake accepts only documents that are 'theirs, unsigned, uncancelled'. So a refused or withdrawn document can never be signed again, and the record keeps saying 'Did not agree' forever.
objections.evidence: §5.2 table, Start row: '`documents` (Sign on this tablet) must be theirs, unsigned, uncancelled'. §8: 'the dentist uses Sign on this tablet on the same document: a new signing, the latest counts, and both are kept'. §5.2 Withdraw requires 'latest signing is agreed'.
objections.fix: Let startIntake accept documents whose latest signing is 'refused', or that have a withdrawal, and are not cancelled. Only a document whose latest state is agreed and not withdrawn is refused. Keep the rule that fields are frozen: a new signing reuses the frozen fields. Add this case to §9 flow 4.

objections.section: 2/5.1 phone path for a patient on file (target 'existing')
objections.problem: For a patient already on file, the phone pages show the record's name and birth date, plus the procedure, teeth and dentist. They are shown to whichever phone presses Start first on a QR displayed on the desk monitor for up to 15 minutes. Anyone in the waiting room who photographs the screen gets health information. At Send, the intake goes straight to 'added' with no desk step, so a stranger's signatures are attached to that patient's record automatically.
objections.evidence: Spec intake_send: `v_done := case when i.target = 'existing' then 'added'`. intake_decide reads `patient.birth_date` for an existing target. §8 'Two phones scan the same code: the first Start wins' is the only check. There is no identity step anywhere in §5.3 or §8.
objections.fix: For target 'existing', the phone must prove who it is before anything is drawn. It types the birth date (or the last 4 digits of the mobile on file), which the definer checks with an attempt cap: 3 misses retire the link as 'replaced'. Until then, intake_view returns only the clinic's face. Alternatively, have an existing-target phone intake end at 'sent', with a one-tap desk confirmation like the new-patient path.

objections.problem: Unlock is specified as authenticate() with login:e: limits. That function finds staff by email only. Members the owner creates (031) may have no email and sign in by username at their clinic's door, so they can never unlock a tablet they parked. The spec also names the page components 'SignInForm pieces', which is the username door form.
objections.evidence: auth.ts:74-83 (`authenticate` … `where s.email = $1`). 031_members.sql:20 (`alter table staff alter column email drop not null`). [clinic]/sign-in.astro:53-58 uses authenticateAt with `login:u:<slug>:<login>`. The auth_event kinds are 'login.ok' and so on (login.astro:65), not 'ok'.
objections.fix: Unlock uses clinicDoor(slug) and authenticateAt(door, login, password), the `login:u:<slug>:<login>` and `login:ip:` limits, and prefills the username from fl_park.s. It logs authEvent('login.ok') plus audit device.unlock. Say plainly where the page lives: /auth/unlock/ is preferable (see the service-worker objection); '[clinic]/unlock.astro' could be read as the public src/pages/[clinic]/ site.

objections.problem: Only `fields` is frozen after a signing or a paper print. The app needs UPDATE on consent_document (patient_id at Add, intake_id on a move, cancelled_at, paper_printed_at, rev), so nothing stated stops it re-pointing a signed document's patient_id, version_id, appointment_id or dentist columns. A bug or a crafted post could move a signed extraction consent to another patient or another visit. 028 closed the same class of hole for forms keys with a trigger.
objections.evidence: Spec §9 checks only 'update consent_document set fields after a signing, or after paper_printed_at, raises'. 028_patient_forms.sql:78-95: clinic_forms_key_guard freezes key, clinic_id, created_at and created_by, and allows only a one-way retire.
objections.fix: Add a BEFORE UPDATE guard. clinic_id, version_id and code never change. patient_id may only go from null to a value, once. intake_id may change only while no signing exists. appointment_id, dentist_id, dentist_prc and fields are frozen once any consent_signing exists or paper_printed_at is set. cancelled_at is refused when a signing exists. Also use column-level grants. Add each of these to the §9 DB checks.

objections.problem: The spec is unclear whether a refusal is thrown or returned. §5.1 declares functions that return `Promise<… | Refused>`, but §5.2 step 7 says refusals throw. Step 6 bumps intake.rev before the checks. If a function returns a Refused and the page does not throw, withClinic commits the bump. The redrawn page then carries the old rev, and the next save always fails with 'Someone else changed these forms'. Also, no shared Refused class exists: four pages each define their own.
objections.evidence: db.ts:95-99 (withClinic commits whatever fn returns). Refused is defined locally in patients/new.astro:124, [patient].astro:173, api/recall.ts:54 and calls/index.astro:54.
objections.fix: Add src/lib/refused.ts with one `Refused` class (reasons: string[]). Every intake.ts and consent-docs.ts function throws it, never returns it. Change the §5.1 return types to drop `| Refused`, or do the rev check last.

objections.section: 5.2 Add as new / Add to a patient on file
objections.problem: addIntake is specified as re-doing addAsNewPatient and addToPatient: 'the addAsNewPatient column mapping' and the 'planFill / TAKEABLE rules'. But planFill, FILLABLE, writeConsents and historyAnswers are private to patient-forms.ts, and the patient insert is inline. Following the spec means a second copy of the fill rules, which will drift from the forms path, for example on the mobile/email ask rule.
objections.evidence: patient-forms.ts:641 (`function planFill`, not exported), the FILLABLE const (not exported), writeConsents (≈505-534, private), historyAnswers (private), and the inline insert at 563-572.
objections.fix: In phase 1, extract shared helpers taking PatientFormValues-shaped answers and a source ({formId} | {intakeId}): insertPatientFromAnswers, fillPatientFromAnswers (planFill), and writeHealthFromAnswers (the lists carried over). Both addAsNewPatient/addToPatient and addIntake call them. Prove with the unchanged scripts/dev/qr-forms/backend-test.mjs.

objections.problem: The claim that server errors log only the intake id is false for /f/i/<token>/. The middleware logs the request path of every thrown error, and the path is the token. The spec also does not say that /f/i/ responses are no-store, and the middleware adds that only for /c/.
objections.evidence: src/middleware.ts:132: console.error(`[error] ${method} ${context.url.pathname}…`). :136 adds no-store only when WORKSPACE (/^\/c\//) matches. /f/[key].astro:55 sets no-store itself.
objections.fix: In the middleware, redact /f/i/<token> (and /f/<key>) to /f/i/… before logging. Add Cache-Control: no-store, X-Robots-Tag: noindex and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer for /^\/f\// in the middleware (or in the page, as /f/[key] does), and state it in §5.3.

objections.problem: The hand-over is 'goLive + claimIntake + parkDevice' in one POST, but these are separate transactions. claimIntake goes through publicRead on another pool connection, so if it runs inside goLive's withClinic callback it cannot see the uncommitted link and returns 'unknown'. The spec also does not say what happens when the claim fails after the link was committed.
objections.evidence: db.ts:106-110 (publicRead is pool.query on its own connection). Spec §5.2: 'Hand-over (same POST, tablet) | goLive + claimIntake + parkDevice'.
objections.fix: Have the desk's browser generate the device secret and let goLive insert the link already claimed (device_hash and claimed_at set) inside its own transaction. The desk is authenticated, so no definer claim is needed. Then park and redirect.

objections.problem: `intake:ip:<ipBucket>` counts every public post and every 30 s ping, across all clinics. A carrier CGNAT address shared by patients at different clinics can therefore lock out real, live links everywhere. The forms deliberately scope their address limit per poster for exactly this reason.
objections.evidence: patient-forms.ts:235-236 ('Per address and poster: one busy carrier address is not every clinic's limit', key forms:ip:<key>:<ip>). throttle.ts comment on LIMITS.forms (CGNAT). Spec: `intake:ip:<ipBucket>` counts 'every public post'; pings every 30 s come to 120 per hour per open page.
objections.fix: Scope the key per clinic (`intake:ip:<clinic>:<bucket>`) and leave pings out of it. The per-link limit, the per-staff creation limit and the device binding already bound abuse by real tokens. Unknown tokens stay on forms:miss.

objections.problem: The photos consent can only be agreed: 'refused' is rejected as invalid. A patient who says no can only choose 'later', which alerts the desk and leaves the form as 'To sign' on the record indefinitely, and the refusal is never recorded. A consent that cannot be declined is not freely given.
objections.evidence: Spec intake_decide: `or (v.code = 'photos' and p_decision <> 'agreed')` raises check_violation, which returns 'invalid'.
objections.fix: Allow 'refused' for photos, recorded as a signed 'Did not agree'. If only some uses are optional, keep them as answers inside an agreed document, and still allow a refusal of the whole.

objections.problem: The owner's flow ends at page 4 with 'end of profile creation'. Q1's default ('no, the desk adds after') changes that requirement without the owner deciding it, and the phone and tablet screens will tell a new patient they are finished when no profile exists yet.
objections.evidence: Relayed user request: '… 4th page consent form, end of profile creation'. Spec §10 Q1, 'Default: no'.
objections.fix: Put Q1 to the owner before phase 2. If the default stays, the patient's thank-you and the desk panel must say plainly that the desk adds the record next. Consider auto-adding at Send when likelyMatches is empty, as the staff member who made the link, and holding only look-alikes for the desk.

objections.section: 7 document page evidence ('read for 2 min 10 s')
objections.problem: read_seconds is decided_at minus intake_page.opened_at. opened_at is set once, when the page is first opened. The resign CTE, intake_send's stale CTE and intake_mark_page's ON CONFLICT all leave it unchanged. After a page-1 edit or a reset, 'read for' includes time spent on other screens, which overstates the evidence on a legal record.
objections.evidence: Spec intake_send: `greatest(0, extract(epoch from (p.decided_at - p.opened_at)))`. The reset UPDATEs in intake_save_page1 and intake_send do not touch opened_at. intake_mark_page's ON CONFLICT updates only state.
objections.fix: Reset opened_at (to null) wherever a page is reset, and set it again on the next 'opened'. Label the evidence 'opened 10:40 · decided 10:42' instead of 'read for'.

objections.problem: The new rule for 'consent to treatment signed' ('a visit_consent row or an agreed general-consent document linked to it') is to be written twice, in VisitStrip and in cal/data.ts's subselect. As worded, it counts a document whose latest signing was later refused or withdrawn.
objections.evidence: src/components/ws/cal/data.ts:75 (`exists (select 1 from visit_consent …) as consent_signed`). visit-consent.ts reads the same thing for the strip. Spec §7: 'The same rule goes into cal/data.ts's consent_signed subselect'.
objections.fix: Add one SQL function in 039, visit_treatment_consented(appointment_id): true when a visit_consent row exists, or when a general document for the visit has an agreed latest signing and no withdrawal after it. Call it from cal/data.ts, VisitStrip and panels.ts.

objections.problem: The check 'exactly one visible .ws-btn-primary per screen' counts nothing on the patient's pages. /f/ pages use .btn.btn-primary, so the one-teal rule goes unmeasured on the screens patients see.
objections.evidence: src/pages/f/[key].astro uses class="btn btn-primary" (2) and "btn btn-quiet" (6), not ws-btn-primary.
objections.fix: Count `.ws-btn-primary, .btn-primary, .entry-btn-primary` (every teal fill class), visible and not disabled, on every screen of /c/…/intake, /f/i/ and unlock.

mAdd.summary: Today a patient is added in-site on ONE page, /c/<slug>/patients/new/ (src/pages/c/[clinic]/patients/new.astro). It has no steps. The page is a single form in panes: Person, Health, Privacy consent (embedded DeskConsent: Not now / At the desk now / Signed on paper), Past visits, Opening balance (money only). There is one teal "Save patient". Everything is written in one withClinic() transaction after lockClinic(): insertPatients, insertHealth, recordDeskConsent or recordPaperConsent, insertVisits, insertMoney. At the top a "Ways to add patients" card links the three ways: Type it in (this page, aria-current), "Patients fill it in" marked Easiest (→ ./qr/, a clinic-wide poster with one live key per clinic, not per patient), and Import a spreadsheet (→ ./import/, the only step-pill wizard in the workspace: Upload · Check · Done). The page only offers the privacy consent (the notice). The one consent to examination and treatment ('treatment-2026-09', TREATMENT_CONSENT) reaches a record in two ways only: (a) the QR patient forms, as patient_consent with channel 'form'; (b) the tablet signing page for a visit (visit_consent, which needs an appointment_id). There are no consent forms per procedure, and no checklist before the QR. The workspace has three step patterns to reuse: import's step pills, the public /f/<key>/ five-step wizard with client-side step checks and a server re-check, and the tablet page's two steps with a "Hand the tablet to <name>" handover. Who may add: records.edit, via canEditRecords → staff_can(). The page checks it at render, on POST, and again inside the transaction.

facts.fact: The page header states the design: one page, clear sections (Person, Health, Consent, Past visits, Opening balance), one Save. Three ways in at the top. Only the name is needed. Everything goes in one form with CSRF, written in ONE withClinic() transaction after lockClinic. A duplicate check runs as the desk types (GET /api/patients/match) and again on Save. Who: canEditRecords; money parts: finance.bill. Audit actions listed.
The page is server-rendered and requires the workspace. money = can(clinic, 'finance.bill'). here = /c/<slug>/patients/new/. The clinic object from requireWorkspace carries perms (Workspace.perms).

The header comment says money is gated by 'canBill in src/lib/invoices.ts'. No such export exists there (grep finds canBill only in record-extra.ts). The code actually uses can(clinic,'finance.bill'), so the comment is stale.

Setup read in one withClinic: area, canEdit (canEditRecords), dentists of this branch (owner/dentist/associate with access or schedule), active procedure_catalog names, HMO suggestions, noticeInForce, the group's DPO name, the next chart no. (nextChartNos over all chart_no), and formsWaiting (countNewForms).
A Refused error class carries reasons[]. The POST runs only when setup.canEdit. csrfOk is checked first; on a miss it redirects 303 to here+'?stale=1', saving nothing.
No-JS 'Add a past visit' posts more=1. The server then just draws one more blank row and saves nothing. The button has formnovalidate.
Rate limit: hit('record:s:'+staffId, ...LIMITS.chart.staff), which is 600 per 60 s.
The person is read by readPersonForm(form). Health and birth date are read by readHealthForm(form, today). Birth-date problems stay unprefixed; other health problems get the prefix 'Health: '.

Past visit rows are validated in full: date not after today or before 1900, service required and at most SERVICE_MAX, dentist from the team or '__other' plus a name, FDI teeth, notes at most VISIT_NOTE_MAX. Money is read only if money is allowed. Paid cannot exceed charged, and the method must be one of PAY_METHODS or 'unrecorded'.
The opening balance (money only) needs an amount and an 'as of' date that is not after today.

Consent choice: consent_how is 'later' | 'desk' | 'paper'. 'desk' needs a notice in force and agreed=1. 'paper' goes through readPaperForm, with problems prefixed 'Consent: '. agreed_as and given_by_name are read.

The transaction runs in this order: re-check canEditRecords, else Refused 'Your account cannot add patients at this branch. Ask the owner.' → lockClinic → snapshot(visitKeys:false) → lookAlikes. A chart no. taken by another patient, or by an archived record, is Refused in words. If any look-alike is not in confirm_new it returns {dupes}. Otherwise it inserts the patient (chartNo = typed or next free), then insertHealth if answered(), then recordDeskConsent or recordPaperConsent (a result other than 'saved' is Refused in words), then past visits (matchService, visitKey, duplicate keys Refused), insertVisits, then insertMoney for visit charges plus the opening balance.

On success it redirects 303 to /c/<slug>/patients/<id>/?saved=new. The duplicate list is mapped for display. A unique violation 23505 becomes 'Another save took the same number…'. A Refused adds its reasons, and anything else is rethrown.
What was typed comes back through val()/list() from the posted FormData. 'Address, emergency contact and more' is a <details> that opens by itself when any of its fields was posted.

The page uses ClinicLayout with section='add-patient' (this lights the Patients tab). 'Back to patients' sits on a small ws-glass card (restoreBackLinks). A CSRF_MESSAGE callout shows on stale. The problems Callout (tone alert, focus, title 'Nothing was saved. N things to fix:', items) shows on refusal.
Someone without canEdit sees only a 'Not allowed' pane saying 'Your account cannot add patients at this branch. Ask the owner.'

THE THREE WAYS: the Pane 'Ways to add patients' (.fm-ways-pane) holds <ul class=fm-ways>. (1) 'Type it in' is a span with aria-current=page and a check mark. (2) 'Patients fill it in' with an 'Easiest' pill links to ./qr/. (3) 'Import a spreadsheet' links to ./import/. When formsWaiting > 0 a line says N patients sent forms from the QR code, with a link to 'New patient forms' (./forms/).
Styling for the three-ways cards: 3 columns from a 46rem container. The chosen card is teal-tint; the others are links with an arrow.

The dupes pane 'Before saving' has role=alert and tabindex=-1 and reads 'This looks like <name>, <mobile>. Open their record?'. Each look-alike has an 'Open record' link. A QUIET button name=confirm_new value=<ids> reads 'It is someone else: save as new'.

Person pane fields: last, first, middle, suffix (datalist), birth_date (with a live age line 'Under 18: a parent or guardian agrees to consent.'), sex radios (SEXES), mobile, email, HMO (datalist), HMO member no. All are autocomplete=off. A live match box (data-match-box) sits beneath them.
The Health pane uses HealthLists (allergies, conditions, medications chips, 'None known'), plus a 'Note for the dentist' textarea.
The Privacy consent pane embeds <DeskConsent embed …> with consents=[], canRecord=true, minor=false, birthKnown=false. The desk chooses who agrees, or the birth-date script picks it.

ONE TEAL BUTTON: 'Save patient' (ws-btn-primary, min-h 48px, full width on phones), with 'Everything is saved together, under your name. If anything needs fixing, nothing is saved.' 'Add a past visit' and 'save as new' are ws-btn-quiet.

Client script: focuses the dupes pane or the problems callout. Enter in one-line inputs does not submit. A beforeunload dirty guard. Health chip logic. The birth date sets the agreed_as radio (<18 gives guardian). consent_how shows or hides the [data-consent-part] blocks. Past visits add, remove and renumber from a <template>. The as-you-type duplicate check debounces 450 ms and calls /api/patients/match.

GET /api/patients/match: session + canOpen. Rate limit schedule:s:. Matches on the same chart no., on the same first and last name with agreeing or missing birth dates, or on the same mobile with the same last name. Up to 5 results, no-store, no CSRF (a GET).

readPersonForm: first AND last names are both required ('Write the last name.' / 'Write the first name.'), each at most 60. Chart no. is at most 20, letters, numbers and ._/-. The mobile must be a PH mobile (normalised to 09…). Email is validated. The emergency phone needs 7 or more digits. Notes are at most 1000. Also suffix tidy, and length caps on HMO and relation. The birth date is NOT read here (readHealthForm reads it).
splitName: 'Last, First' or 'First … Last' with Filipino particles (dela, de los, san…) starting the surname and Jr./Sr./II… as the suffix. A single word is a last name alone.

splitName is used by the import plan and by the booking panel's new-patient insert in POST /api/schedule. That insert takes a one-word name as first name with last '—', a chart from nextChartNo, and audit patient.create.
snapshot(tx, groupId): every patient (archived kept apart), takenCharts including archived ones, archivedByChart, dentists, services, and maps byChart, byPhoneName and byName.
archivedChart returns the sentence 'Chart no. X belongs to an archived record (…), so it is not used again.'
lookAlikes: the same chart no.; the same name when the birth dates agree or either is missing; the same mobile with the same last name. At most 5.
lockClinic = pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(clinicId)), the schedule's and booking's own lock.
nextChartNos(taken, n) gives P-0001 style numbers, stepping past taken ones.
insertPatients: one insert via jsonb_to_recordset (created_by = staff, import_id). Returns ids in order. Audits patient.create for each.
insertHealth: a first medical_history version with answered_by 'staff', recorded_by staff, only when there is none yet. Audit health.update.

Other patient insert paths: public web booking (chart 'W-nnnn') and forms 'Add as a new patient' (addAsNewPatient: lockClinic, likelyMatches, nextChartNos, patient row with guardian fields and occupation, medical_history answered_by 'patient' with form_id, writeConsents, form marked added).
canEditRecords(tx, staffId, clinicId) runs `select staff_can($1,$2,'records.edit')`. It is read inside the writing transaction.

Permission keys: 'records.edit' = 'Add and edit patients, health history, consent and charts'. All six DEFAULT_ROLES hold records.edit. finance.bill belongs to Owner, Admin and Secretary. permsOf: can_view_finance adds finance.bill and finance.money; can_edit_records=false removes records.edit. can(ws,key) reads ws.perms.

Entry points to Add patient: the Patients list shows the teal '+ Add patient' with Import quiet beside it, only when canEdit. The shell's New menu (quiet) always shows Add patient: links.addPatient comes from routes.ts and is not permission-gated, so the page itself refuses. Also the search empty state and the booking panel hint.

recordDeskConsent: locks the patient FOR UPDATE and needs a notice in force equal to the posted version. The who and minor rules apply (under 18 → guardian, who must be named). One consent per notice, unless a guardian's is being added. Inserts patient_consent with channel 'desk' and audit consent.desk. Results: none | no-notice | changed | already | saved | who | minor | guardian-name.

recordPaperConsent: 'clinic' → a patient_paper_consent row (one per day, audit consent.paper_form). 'notice' → patient_consent with channel 'paper' and signed_on, refused if signed before effective_from, with the minor rule applied as of the signing day (audit consent.paper). readPaperForm reads the paper_* fields. PAPER_WORDS holds the sentences.
noticeInForce reads current_consent_version() (privacy only since 028). isMinor gives under 18 on the Manila calendar. readConsents lists privacy consents only.

DeskConsent embed mode: no form tag, no CSRF, no intent. Three pk-card radios, consent_how later/desk/paper ('The record asks at the next visit' / 'Show them the notice on this screen' / 'Record the date on the paper'). The desk and paper blocks are [data-consent-part] and hidden when not chosen.

DeskConsent 'Show the patient' facing mode: the panel fills the screen, everything else is made inert, and Tab is trapped. 'Done reading' leads to 'Please hand the screen back to the desk', then 'Back to the form'. Enter is blocked while facing. WORDS switch the labels by who (patient / guardian / unknown). SHORT holds a plain summary of privacy-2026-09.
DeskConsent's teal 'Record consent' is drawn only when not embedded, so Add patient keeps a single teal button. The facing-mode 'Done reading' is teal, but only while the rest of the page is hidden.

Import wizard: three steps on one page with the step in the address (?id=), shown as pills (STEPS = Upload, Check, Done; .imp-steps with aria-current=step and data-done). One teal button per step: 'Read the file', 'Import …', 'Import another file'. CSRF is checked first (on a miss, ?stale=1). canEditRecords is re-checked on POST.

The QR page /patients/qr/ is 'one screen, one teal button' (Print poster). It is gated by canEditRecords. formsKey gives ONE live key per clinic (clinic_forms_key), created the first time the page is opened. newFormsKey retires it (CSRF, audit forms.key_new). formsNoticeReady gates production.
The patient forms are closed in production: FORMS_PRIVACY_VERSIONS is empty.

Public forms wizard /f/<key>/ has five steps (about, health, teeth, cards, consent) built from STEPS data. The script shows one step at a time: Continue runs check(at) (the server's parser), Back is a button, completed steps in the stepper are buttons, and popstate walks the steps. Without the script it is one long form. Nothing is redirected on error.

There is only ONE consent to examination and treatment: TREATMENT_CONSENT['treatment-2026-09'] (title, 6 points, tick). consent_version.kind is checked to 'privacy'|'treatment'. The app cannot insert, update or delete consent_version: wording is migration-only.

Forms consents are written as patient_consent rows with channel 'form', one for privacy_version and one for treatment_version, one per version per patient, with the minor rule applied. Audit consent.form.

Tablet signing /patients/<id>/sign/<visit>/ is two steps on one page, with no workspace shell. The clinic step ticks plan lines, notes 'anything else' and picks the dentist, then 'Hand the tablet to <name>' (teal). mSign.summary:
Today there is exactly ONE treatment consent (consent_version 'treatment-2026-09', words only in code in TREATMENT_CONSENT), signed two ways: (a) by hand on the clinic tablet, per VISIT, into the insert-only visit_consent table (035) with the strokes, a free-text 'treatment' (<=600 chars), dentist_id, signer and relation; (b) as a typed name on the public QR forms, which become patient_consent rows (channel 'form') only when the desk adds the form. The privacy notice is separate (patient_consent rows, kind 'privacy', read by readConsents/consentInForce). Add patient (new.astro) takes only the privacy consent (desk or paper) and no treatment consent at all.

For several procedure-specific consent forms signed at once when a patient is added, each with clinic-filled fields, the current model blocks you in six places:
1. visit_consent.appointment_id is NOT NULL (035:20), and a new patient has no visit.
2. consent_version.kind allows only 'privacy'|'treatment' (028:106). The 035 trigger demands kind='treatment' (035:42), and treatmentInForce/current_consent_of return a single version per kind, so there is no idea of several forms in force at once.
3. There are no columns for procedure, teeth, anaesthesia or estimate. The only slot is 'treatment' text of up to 600 chars (035:22), plus dentist_id with ON DELETE SET NULL, whose name is re-read live from staff (visit-consent.ts:75-78).
4. The exact words are not stored with the signature. consent_version has only title and summary (012:31-37), and the paragraphs and tick live in a TS map (patient-forms-def.ts:216-229). The forms printout already falls back to "version X: agreed" when words are missing (forms/[form]/print.astro:184-186).
5. No print route exists for a tablet-signed consent.
6. The QR route has a per-clinic key, not a per-patient one; it takes a typed-name signature, no strokes, and is closed in production.

What is needed:
- A new migration (039+) that adds a per-form code to consent_version and widens its kind check.
- Seeded, migration-only words with a body/hash (the app can only select consent_version: 028:136-137).
- A new insert-only signing table (or two: signing + one row per form), with appointment_id nullable, the filled fields as jsonb, a frozen snapshot of the words as rendered plus the fields and a sha256, and the dentist's name and PRC as they were at signing, following 035's RLS, grants and trigger pattern.
- A signIntake() that runs in new.astro's one-transaction pattern.
- A multi-step page that reuses the sign page's pad, handover and thank-you screens.
- An A5 print route in the letters/rx pattern.
- The record's Consent tab, VisitPanels, Timeline, VisitStrip and the calendar's consent_signed made to read the new rows.

Design caveat to raise with the owner: docs/clinic-operations.md:59 says consent should be per procedure and per visit, not a paragraph signed at registration.

Prices on consent are fee-guide estimates, not statements (CLAUDE.md 033).
gaps: visit_consent.appointment_id is NOT NULL (035:20), the trigger requires a matching appointment (035:39-41), and canSign requires a visit id (visit-record.ts:80-81). A consent signed while adding a patient has no visit, so this needs either a new table with a nullable appointment_id, or an ALTER in a new migration plus a replaced trigger function. The alternative is to create or attach today's visit (the 036 'Here now' walk-in path).

No column for procedure, teeth (structured), anaesthesia, estimate, alternatives or procedure-specific risks exists in any consent table. visit_consent has one free-text 'treatment' of at most 600 chars (035:22; visit-consent.ts:133-136), too small for several filled forms.

consent_version.kind allows only 'privacy'|'treatment' (028:106). The 035 trigger demands 'treatment' (035:42), and treatmentInForce (visit-consent.ts:60-65) and current_consent_of (028:124-132) return ONE version per kind. Several procedure forms in force at once need a per-form code (e.g. consent_version.code) and an 'in force per code' function.

The exact words are NOT stored with a signature: consent_version holds only title and summary (012:31-37), and the paragraphs and tick live in a TS map (patient-forms-def.ts:216-229). Reprinting years later depends on nobody ever editing or removing that map; forms/[form]/print.astro:184-186 already falls back to 'version X: agreed'. Recommend a frozen snapshot per signed form (the rendered words plus the filled fields as JSON/text, and a sha256), and/or a body column on consent_version seeded by migration.

The dentist's name is not snapshotted: visit_consent.dentist_id is ON DELETE SET NULL (035:23) and names are joined live from staff (visit-consent.ts:75-78). A renamed or removed dentist changes or blanks old consents. Store the name and PRC as they were at signing.
There is no print route for tablet-signed consents; a new patients/<id>/consents/<id>/ A5 page is needed.
One signature covering all forms, or one signature per form, is an owner and legal decision. The current model is one row per signing.

The QR route cannot carry a staff checklist. The key is per clinic, not per patient (028:52-63). The public submit is a definer function with no staff or patient context. Its signature is a typed name, not strokes (patient-forms-def.ts:479-480; 028:169). It is closed in production (patient-forms.ts:144). Putting chosen forms in front of the QR scanner needs a per-intake one-time token (new table plus definer functions), stroke capture on the phone, and the privacy notice update.
Consents tied to a QR form that is never added are purged at 30 days (028:413).

The owner's request (sign procedure consents at patient creation) is in tension with docs/clinic-operations.md:59, which says consent is per procedure and per visit, not signed at registration, and asks for a 'plan changed since consent' warning. Raise this with the owner: at intake the procedure may not yet be decided.
patient_consent is not insert-only (the 002:128 default privileges were never revoked for it), unlike visit_consent. A new consent table must revoke explicitly.
The record, Timeline, VisitPanels, VisitStrip and calendar only understand visit_consent and TREATMENT_CONSENT. New procedure consents will read as 'No signed consent' unless they are wired in.
No procedure-specific consent words exist anywhere in the repo (only the general treatment-2026-09), so they must be drafted and reviewed by a dentist and the lawyer.
